hypothesis: completeCartWorkflow guards against double completion with acquireLockStep, but the default locking provider is InMemoryLockingProvider, which is per process. With target.servers 2 on one database, two concurrent complete calls for the same cart on different servers can both see no order_cart link (the check happens before any order is created) and each create an order. That would break one_order_per_cart (two distinct orders for one cart) and possibly no_orphaned_orders. Expect at least some runs to fail one_order_per_cart; SOLO has 1 unit, so no_oversell may also trip if both orders reserve it.
submitted_scenario:
schema: oversold.scenario/v1
name: same-cart-two-servers
description: One cart holding one SOLO unit is completed at the same time on both servers.
target:
  engine: medusa
  version: 2.22.0
  servers: 2
stock:
  SOLO: 1
carts:
  alice:
    server: 1
    lines:
    - sku: OVS-SOLO
      qty: 1
race:
- id: alice-on-server-1
  server: 1
  do: complete
  cart: alice
- id: alice-on-server-2
  server: 2
  do: complete
  cart: alice
timing:
  release: together
  jitter_ms:
  - 0
  - 3
  request_timeout_ms: 30000
faults: []
runs: 20
seed: 7

hypothesis: Control: same cart completed twice on one server. The in-memory lock should serialize the two calls within the process, so the second should see the order_cart link and return the same order (or fail). Expect no check to fail, which would show that any failure in attempt 1 comes from the cross-server case.
